status: OPEN — root cause identified, fix not yet implemented
found: 2026-08-08, by wrapped_log_survives_remount after the circular allocator landed
symptom: All 16 keys readable before close; 0 of 16 readable after reopening from flash. The checkpoint restores the index correctly (index_len=16) and tail replay applies 0 records, so the index is intact — but every offset in it addresses erased flash.

evidence.note: Delta is constant across records but is NOT a whole number of segments, so it is not a simple segment-base rebase. The same logical records exist at both addresses; the index tracks the older copy.

reclaim_trace: Every compaction reports relocated=0 while 16 keys are live. Segment 7 holds the newest copies and is erased anyway, because the liveness test compares the scanned record offset against the index candidates and they never match.
ruled_out: Scan starting on the segment header — compact_one_async already skips the header page when read_header succeeds (has_header=true in the trace).
Append/program offset mismatch — traced APPEND offset=913500 head=913152 batch_off=348 against PROGRAM addr=913408, i.e. the byte does land inside the programmed page.
Checkpoint capturing unflushed batch offsets — flush_pending_batches_async was added to both checkpoint paths; symptom unchanged.
Head roll invalidating buffered offsets — flush_before_roll_async was added to roll_head_async; symptom unchanged.
likely_cause: Records relocated by compaction are re-appended to the cold log, but the index is not updated to the new offset, or is updated against a head position that later moves. The index then names a location that a subsequent reclaim erases.
next_step: Instrument reappend_cold and the index upsert that follows it: confirm whether the post-relocation index_update_offset runs, and whether the offset it stores is computed before or after the cold head rolls.
